queue.result: Done, iteration 2. Occurrence #8 read first-hand (gh run view 34164645184 --log-failed): sha 15ce482, on MASTER (a first -- removes the reading that F292 is a property of the cycle branches' trees), hub-test the only failure, 3968 passed / 1 error, ERROR at setup of test_flow_fires_a_review_turn.py::test_a_review_that_cannot_be_prepared_does_not_become_an_ordinary_turn on DROP TABLE requirement_drift at conftest.py:473. Registry printed its FIFTH identical negative. New numbers: failure at progress [33%], not [66%]; and 30.7s between the previous test passing and the error, i.e. the whole busy_timeout, so the holder held throughout. THE FINDING: the entry's leading conclusion -- that the registry's negatives FALSIFY a product-engine connection as the holder, n=4/n=5 -- is TOO STRONG. sqlalchemy 2.0.50 pool/base.py:877-886 fires dispatch.close BEFORE attempting the close and unconditionally, and _close_connection (371-384) and _finalize_fairy (1006-1011) swallow close/reset failures into the sqlalchemy.pool logger, which pytest discards for a passing test. So a product-engine connection still holding the file is GUARANTEED to print 'no connection checked out'. Plus a silent leak path: aiosqlite has_terminate=True, so the discard path calls Connection.stop(), which merely QUEUES the only real sqlite3 close onto the worker thread and returns a future nobody awaits (aiosqlite/core.py:116-132) -- if that thread is not draining, nothing closes and nothing raises. COUNTER-EVIDENCE, and it is the sharpest constraint: both readable CI occurrences (34164645184, 34029310406) contain ZERO PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning, zero 'Event loop is closed', zero GC non-checked-in-connection warnings, and hub/pyproject.toml sets no filterwarnings -- so in those two the worker thread did not visibly crash, and F295's fix should NOT be expected to close F292. F279 answered explicitly: NOT the same class (different exception, locus, latency, and opposite reproducibility) but shares a cause of opportunity in agent_trigger.py:1190's un-awaited _execute_run task. Recorded in the day log AND appended to FINDINGS.md's F292 entry as its eighth-occurrence section; the entry's Status line deliberately left for d1b.
